title: Show your work
lede: Quibi was a private company and never published accounts or a subscriber count. Almost every figure on this page is therefore a press report, a company statement to the press or a third-party estimate, and is labelled that way. The primary documents are the founders’ open letter, Roku’s annual reports and the rivals’ own filings.

notes.label: No audited figures
notes.text: Quibi was privately held. It filed nothing with the SEC and never published a subscriber count, revenue or a profit and loss account. The number of paying subscribers on the day it closed is **unknown**; figures that circulate for it are not used on this page.

notes.label: Press-reported figures
notes.text: The $1.75B raised is the company’s own statement to Variety.[^3] The 7.4 million first-year subscriber target, the projection of fewer than 2 million, the $300M budget cut, the $1B expected to be spent by the third quarter of 2020 and the further $200M the company expected to need are all from a Wall Street Journal report of June 14, 2020. We could not open the Journal’s article and cite it through Tubefilter, Señal News and TechSpot.[^7][^8] The New York Times gives the first-year plan as “seven million users and $250 million in subscriber revenue” and planned marketing of $470M.[^5] The roughly $350M returned to investors is reported, not confirmed by the company: Variety says Quibi “reportedly told investors” of that amount and Deadline says there was “around $350 million still in the bank.”[^2][^16] The price Roku paid was not disclosed; “less than $100 million” is the Wall Street Journal’s figure, repeated by Variety’s source as “significantly” less than $100 million.[^16][^19]

notes.label: Estimates
notes.text: All Sensor Tower download and conversion numbers are that firm’s **estimates** from app-store data, not counts: 379,000 installs on launch day, 2.9 million by May 11, 3.8 million by June 7, about 4.5 million by July 8, about 9.6 million by October 21, and 72,000 paying users out of about 910,000 early sign-ups.[^5][^7][^9][^12] Quibi disputed them and gave higher totals of its own (1.7 million in week one, 3.5 million in May, 5 million in June, more than 5.6 million in July).[^5][^6][^7][^9] TechCrunch gives 300,000 for launch-day downloads on iOS.[^14] The $5.6M cost of a 30-second Super Bowl spot is Quartz’s figure for the going rate, not a price Quibi disclosed.[^24]

notes.label: Derived figures
notes.text: **198 days** from launch to the wind-down announcement is April 6 to October 21, 2020; **239 days** of service is April 6 to December 1, 2020 (“on or about”).[^10][^15] **$1.4B not returned** = $1.75B raised − about $350M reportedly returned; it is a remainder, not an audited cost, and ignores whatever Roku paid.[^3][^16] **250 Super Bowl slots** = $1.4B ÷ $5.6M.[^24] **About $5.9M a day** = $1.4B ÷ 239 days. **Average daily installs** between estimate dates are differences between successive Sensor Tower totals divided by the days between them: (2.9M − 0.379M) ÷ 35 = about 72,000; (3.8M − 2.9M) ÷ 27 = about 33,000; (4.5M − 3.8M) ÷ 31 = about 23,000; (9.6M − 4.5M) ÷ 105 = about 49,000. The **8%** conversion rate is 72,000 ÷ 910,000, as stated by The Verge.[^9] The **5.4 million shortfall** is 7.4M − 2M.[^8]

notes.label: Disputed or unverified
notes.text: Vulture reports that in market research 70% of respondents thought Quibi was a food-delivery service; a Quibi executive denied the account, and we treat it as **unverified**.[^4] Vulture also reports studio investments “in the $20 million range” and a “round-tripping” arrangement that a Quibi executive denied.[^4] Ad commitments are given as $150M by Variety and $100M by Vulture.[^3][^4] Staff numbers are approximate: Deadline says “200-strong,” Cartoon Brew “200-odd.”[^2][^32] The claim that Meg Whitman threatened to resign is the Wall Street Journal’s, cited through The Verge.[^11]

notes.label: The name today
notes.text: Quibi’s holding company was renamed QBI Holdings and existed in September 2021 only to settle the Eko case.[^21] The shows are branded Roku Originals.[^17] We found no product or service operating under the Quibi name. Our request to quibi.com in October 2026 was refused by the server, so the present content of the domain is **unknown**; the last archived page we captured, from June 2021, pointed to The Roku Channel.[^36]

notes.label: Rivals’ figures are not like for like
notes.text: Disney+ is paid subscribers at October 3, 2020.[^33] HBO Max is activations at the end of 2020, most of them existing HBO customers.[^34] Peacock is sign-ups, including free accounts, as of January 28, 2021.[^35] Apple did not publish a figure for Apple TV+.

notes.label: General knowledge
notes.text: Disney+ launched in the United States on November 12, 2019, Apple TV+ on November 1, 2019, HBO Max on May 27, 2020 and Peacock nationally on July 15, 2020. Super Bowl LIV was played on February 2, 2020. Jeffrey Katzenberg was chairman of Walt Disney Studios and a co-founder of DreamWorks; Meg Whitman was chief executive of eBay and of Hewlett-Packard.

notes.label: Videos
notes.text: Upload dates are taken from each YouTube watch page. The Super Bowl spot is a third-party upload made on the day of the game; the CES keynote is on the CES channel; the two CNBC clips and the Good Morning America segment are on the broadcasters’ own channels.
